evals.prompt: Copilot left review comments on the Crash Course parallelization page in my docs PR. The comments are in .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-address-review-comments/evals/files/copilot-comments.md and the page as it stands now is .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-address-review-comments/evals/files/crash-course-parallelization.md (treat it as docs/python/getting-started/crash-course/parallelization.md at DOC-857 commit f2ef483084). Go through the comments and tell me which ones to take, what to change, and draft a reply for each. Don't edit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A triage of 10 real-pattern Copilot comments on a Tutorial page: apply the four real defects (C1-C3, and C9's takeaway fixed at tutorial resolution rather than by listing conditions), decline the title-case change (corpus convention), keep configuration detail out of the tutorial narrative, decline enlarging the example, keep a claim the source supports, and draft reasoned replies.
expectations: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments

Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)

For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)

Treats C9 as a defect to fix (apply, or apply with a different fix): proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties. Declining C9, or offering the rewording only as optional, fails

For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason
